sentences.text: Petitioner is the accused in C.C.No.526 of 2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Hosdurg.

sentences.text:
The case arises out of Crime No.1023 of 2015 of Hosdurg Police Station,
Kasaragod.

The prosecution alleges that the accused had collected an amount of Rs.40,00,000/-
promising a medical seat in a medical college for the daughter of the defacto complainant and thereafter failed to arrange the seat or return the amount and thereby committed the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
Sri.Abdul Raoof Pallipath, the learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the prosecution allegations are totally false and the offences as alleged are not at all attracted.

It is further submitted that even if the allegations are assumed to be true, still it cannot make out any offence as the complainant is alleged to have attempted to procure a seat by illegal means and therefore they cannot thereafter turn around and allege an offence against the petitioner.

Notwithstanding the above, the learned CRL.MC NO. 7750 OF 2024 2024:KER:70353 counsel submitted that, the uncontroverted allegations at the most would only indicate a civil liability and therefore the prosecution of the petitioner is without any basis.

3. Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, contended that the uncontroverted allegations clearly make out the offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating and therefore this is a matter for trial.
4. On a perusal of the final report, it is revealed that the crime case is of the year 2015.
The uncontroverted allegations do prima facie make out the offences alleged.
However, whether the prosecution is able to prove the allegation or not is a matter which can be decided only after trial.

2 5.

In the decision in Mahendra K.C. v. State of Karnataka and Others [(2022) 2 SCC 129], the Supreme Court has reiterated that the exercise of jurisdiction under the inherent powers of this Court must be resorted to only sparingly and cautiously that too when manifest injustice occur if such power is not exercised.

entities.text: Mahendra K.C. v. State of Karnataka and Others [(2022) 2 SCC 129]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. The circumstances in the instant case do not reveal that any manifest injustice would be meted out to the petitioner especially since the case is of the year 2015 and the trial can be CRL.MC NO.
7750 OF 2024 2024:KER:70353 commenced without undue delay.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere in exercise of the powers under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Sd/-
